This confirms the invariant is preserved. The C# binding forwards the caller's `cellIndices` and `numCells` unchanged into `recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs`, with no dedup step in `Ckzg.cs`, but the core C function itself rejects duplicates before `vanishing_polynomial_for_missing_cells` (in `src/eip7594/recovery.c`) is ever reached.

The strict-ascending-order check in `recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs` in `src/eip7594/eip7594.c` (lines 202-213) requires `cell_indices[i] > cell_indices[i-1]` for all `i > 0`. A duplicated pair `(k, k)` violates this because `cell_indices[i] == cell_indices[i-1]`, causing `C_KZG_BADARGS` to be returned immediately — well before `recover_cells` (`src/eip7594/recovery.c:200`) or `vanishing_polynomial_for_missing_cells` (`src/eip7594/recovery.c:93`) execute. The repo's own test vector `recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs_case_invalid_duplicate_cell_index` (`tests/recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs/kzg-mainnet/recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs_case_invalid_duplicate_cell_index/data.yaml`) explicitly encodes `cell_indices: [1, 1, 2, 3, ...]` with `output: null`, confirming this is the intended and verified reference behavior shared across implementations (this test format is shared with the Rust/Go/other bindings' reference test suites).

Consequently:
- `vanishing_polynomial_for_missing_cells` is never invoked with duplicate-derived missing-index data because the malformed input never reaches `recover_cells`.
- The C# binding (`bindings/csharp/Ckzg.Bindings/Ckzg.cs:262-280`, calling into `bindings/csharp/ckzg_wrap.c`) has `ThrowOnError` mapping `C_KZG_BADARGS` to `ArgumentException` (`Ckzg.cs:317-328`), so Nethermind (or any C# consumer) observes a clean, deterministic exception rather than divergent output.
- The int→UInt64 cast of `numCells` in the C# wrapper does not affect this path, since the ascending-order check operates purely on the `cell_indices` array contents, independent of the `numCells` type width, and negative `numCells` would already be rejected by `ThrowOnInvalidLength` span-size checks before reaching native code.

Both sides of the claimed equality (`Z(x)` roots vs. missing columns' evaluation points) are never computed under this input because the function returns `C_KZG_BADARGS` first; there is no divergence to trigger, and the guard (`i > 0 && cell_indices[i] <= cell_indices[i - 1]`) is exactly the strictly-ascending/no-duplicates check that closes this class of bug.     public static unsafe void RecoverCellsAndKzgProofs(Span<byte> recoveredCells, Span<byte> recoveredProofs,
            ReadOnlySpan<UInt64> cellIndices, ReadOnlySpan<byte> cells, int numCells, IntPtr ckzgSetup)
    {
        ThrowOnUninitializedTrustedSetup(ckzgSetup);
        ThrowOnInvalidLength(recoveredCells, nameof(recoveredCells), BytesPerCell * CellsPerExtBlob);
        ThrowOnInvalidLength(recoveredProofs, nameof(recoveredProofs), BytesPerProof * CellsPerExtBlob);
        ThrowOnInvalidLength(cellIndices, nameof(cellIndices), numCells);
        ThrowOnInvalidLength(cells, nameof(cells), BytesPerCell * numCells);

        fixed (byte* recoveredCellsPtr = recoveredCells, recoveredProofsPtr = recoveredProofs, cellsPtr = cells)
        {
            fixed(UInt64* cellIndicesPtr = cellIndices)
            {
                KzgResult result = RecoverCellsAndKzgProofs(recoveredCellsPtr, recoveredProofsPtr, cellIndicesPtr,
                    cellsPtr, (UInt64)numCells, ckzgSetup);
                ThrowOnError(result);
            }
        }
    }

    private static void ThrowOnError(KzgResult result)
    {
        switch (result)
        {
            case KzgResult.BadArgs: throw new ArgumentException();
            case KzgResult.Malloc: throw new InsufficientMemoryException();
            case KzgResult.Ok:
                return;
            default:
                throw new ApplicationException("KZG returned unexpected result");
        }
    }
